jobs.description:
About Peraton

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Program Overview

Provide critical communications and tracking for multiple spacecraft from three complexes located globally, and operates year round 24 hours/7days to provide continuous contact with the spacecraft. The program fulfills NASA goals by supporting NASA deep space mission set, including NASA-funded missions and collaborative international missions.

About The Role

We are looking for a Lead Safety & Environmental Analyst
to support our Deep Space Network (DSN) Operations and Maintenance O&M contract with the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and NASA in Fort Irwin, CA.

What You'll Do:

As Lead Safety & Environmental Analyst, your primary responsibility is ensuring the safety of personnel working in and around complex antenna, mechanical, and electrical systems at a remote government facility. You will lead safety programs, investigate incidents, drive risk reduction, and maintain regulatory compliance across the full spectrum of EHS disciplines - with a clear emphasis on occupational safety first.

Core Safety Responsibilities:

Lead and continuously improve site safety programs, with emphasis on high-hazard work (electrical, elevated, confined space, heavy equipment)
Conduct and lead incident investigations; identify root causes and drive corrective actions to closure
Conduct hazard assessments, job safety analysis (JSAs), and Management of Change (MOC) reviews
Perform and lead EHS audits, field observations, and self-assessments; report findings to leadership
Lead or support emergency response planning and exercises
Analyze safety performance data (OSHA 300 logs, LTIR, frequency rates) and present trends to stakeholders

Training & Compliance:

Develop and deliver EHS training programs; certify trainers where applicable (OSHA 500/501)
Ensure compliance with federal and California regulations (OSHA, Cal/OSHA, EPA, Cal/EPA, NFPA, APCD)
Manage Air Quality and Water programs, including regulatory reporting and agency coordination
Prepare internal and external compliance reports, including data analysis and trend summaries

Collaboration & Communication:

Serve as the primary EHS point of contact for site management, trade personnel, and JPL/NASA stakeholders
Represent the program in discussions with regulatory agencies and community stakeholders
Provide guidance and mentorship to junior EHS staff

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

BS/BA + 8 years of experience; MS/MA + 6 years; PhD + 3 years; or 4 years of directly relevant experience in lieu of degree
Strong knowledge of OSHA, Cal/OSHA, EPA, NIOSH, NFPA, and APCD regulations; NASA familiarity is a plus
Demonstrated experience leading safety programs in complex industrial or government facility environments
Experience with construction safety oversight and managing shifting project priorities
Ability to analyze EHS data and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
Valid California driver's license (Read-ID)
U.S. citizenship required; must pass background check and NCIC screening

Preferred Qualifications:

Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or OHST/CHST (BCSP)
OSHA 500/501 Train-the-Trainer certification
Prior experience in government or DOD facility contracts

Demonstrated experience coordinating multidisciplinary project teams, managing technical tasks, and communicating technical findings and recommendations to clients, regulators, and other project stakeholders; strong proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

Job Description

Are you eager to develop your excellence in an inclusive, collaborative, and empowering community? Are you excited about joining a company that strives to make a difference – for its employees, clients, and society? Are you motivated by creating sustainable change that benefits society and nature?

If this sounds like you, or you’re curious to learn more, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our Environment & Health team and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.

Your new role

We invite you to bring your environmental consulting experience into play as you support provide technical and project leadership for environmental investigation and remediation projects in the New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Metropolitan areas. In this position, the selected candidate will lead and support multidisciplinary teams working closely with Professional Engineers (PEs), Professional Geologists (PGs), Licensed Site Remediation Professionals (LSRPs) and other technical specialists.

As a senior member of the team, you will apply your technical expertise and professional judgment to guide site investigation and remediation strategies, oversee field programs and data evaluation, prepare and review technical deliverables, and support regulatory and client communications. You will also provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior and mid-level staff while helping ensure projects are completed efficiently, safely, and in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

The position provides opportunities to work on a diverse range of projects involving, geologic and environmental investigations, conceptual site model development, remedial strategy and design, data evaluation and modelling, regulatory compliance and technical reporting.

Your key tasks and responsibilities for this role will be:

Lead and oversee geologic and site investigations, including Remedial Investigations, Feasibility Studies, Remedial Designs, Remedial Actions, and post-remediation OM&M; plan and oversee various drilling methodologies and investigation techniques, including monitoring well installations, packer testing, groundwater sampling, and vapor intrusion investigations.
Oversee and review detailed and accurate field and project documentation; manage and successfully track field and project activities related to scope, schedule, and budget.
Serve as a key technical point of contact for clients and project stakeholders, communicating investigation findings, technical recommendations, project status, and emerging issues; participate in client meetings and work collaboratively with LSRP and technical leads to develop practical solutions that meet project and client objectives.
Coordinate the development and finalization through final submission of technical documents, including regulatory reports, work plans, and biennial remedial action protectiveness submittals, pursuant to regulatory requirements; independently develop scopes of work and budgetary cost estimates and support initial project setup, invoicing, and project closeout.
Proactively communicate change management needs during project execution; provide technical guidance and mentorship to early-career and mid-level Geological Scientists and contribute to the development of team capabilities and technical best practices.

Qualifications

About you

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Geology, Geological Science, Environmental Science, or related field, with 7+ years of relevant experience.
Possession, eligibility, or demonstrated progress toward obtaining, a PG license and/or LSRP.
At a minimum, 40-Hour OSHA HAZWOPER certification and up-to-date 8-hour refresher; additional OSHA health and safety training and certifications are a plus.
Strong working knowledge of federal, PA, NJ, and NY environmental and site remediation regulations, with demonstrated experience applying regulatory requirements to investigation and remediation projects.
Demonstrated experience coordinating multidisciplinary project teams, managing technical tasks, and communicating technical findings and recommendations to clients, regulators, and other project stakeholders; strong proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Investment in your development
Being valued for the unique person you are
Never being short of inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Position Summary

We have an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Project Coordinator.

The Department of Population Health at the NYU Grossman School of Medicine seeks a Project Coordinator with experience in complex project management to work across a multidisciplinary team to track, initiate, manage, and complete major projects associated with the City Health Dashboard and Congressional District Health Dashboard. Under the supervision of the Assistant Director, this position will also be required to liaise with external parties to communicate budget and project priorities. The Dashboards are interactive data and mapping websites developed by NYU Langone Health to help US policymakers, community-based organizations, journalists, and others leverage the power of data to improve health and well-being.

The team that updates and maintains the City Health Dashboard and Congressional District Health Dashboard consists of data, communications, partnership, and policy specialists. This role works with all members of that team, including external web developer consultants, to track and coordinate deliverables across weeks and months of the project. The most complex deliverables include data releases and website feature updates. On both websites, the team releases new years of data or new features more than three times per year. This role is responsible for supporting the intricate planning of these releases and monitoring the progress of all 20+ stakeholders. Planning for these releases involves brainstorming with team leadership, crafting project charters and presentations, creating work plans in MS tools, monitoring feedback in JIRA, and communicating progress in team meetings.

Utilizing, innovating, and augmenting a complex set of interdependent Microsoft tools to track, visualize, and manage timelines and deliverables, assist with progress reporting, and support the completion of grant deliverables. Working with internal and external parties to organize multiple projects and project components. Presenting project and release timelines to all team members and leadership and closely monitoring project progress to flag any potential delays or changes.
Monitoring project budgets and expected estimates to flag overspending or the need for resource reallocation within our web developer contract and budget.
Collaborating with team members responsible for public health communication, data analysis, and website development and translating project priorities and decisions from team leadership.
